newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan plans stock exchange reforms.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan plans stock exchange reforms.

text.p: Pakistan will restructure its three stock exchanges and revamp its regulatory authority as part of a modernising drive aimed at attracting more foreign investment, a senior official said on Thursday.

Shamim Ahmed Khan, chairman of the state Corporate Law Authority (CLA), told Reuters the CLA had told the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) to change the composition of its board to bring in professionals not involved in the equity market. He said the government was also planning to restructure the CLA to give it the functions of a securities commission.

"That process is on and we should be having a draft law by early July, which will be seen by the government, and then go to the parliament for enactment," he said. "The changes are not just for the stock exchanges. I would like to impose discipline on ourselves also," he added.
The CLA gave the KSE a directive on Wednesday asking it to amend its rules by July 31 to incorporate the changes sought by the CLA so that one third of its board would be non-brokers.

It also asked the KSE to appoint a CLA-approved full-time professional non-broker as its chief executive officer, who would also act as president of the stock exchange. The board of directors would elect a separate chairman.
Khan said similar instructions would soon be sent to the smaller Lahore and Islamabad stock exchanges.

"The CLA has initiated the process of major restructuring of the stock exchanges which should modernise the infrastructure of the market," he said. "These measures are aimed at modernising the stock exchanges and making them more transparent and responsive to the interest of the general public."
The KSE has been asked to reduce the size of its board to 12 members from 15 and add four CLA-nominated professionals. Khan said these might be accountants, bankers or lawyers.
He said the restructuring would bring Pakistan's bourses into line with practices in other emerging and regional markets.
He said the CLA had also set up two committees to examine the practice of short-selling -- common in Pakistani bourses -- and to review the capital adequacy of active brokers.
Khan said the committees, set up on Tuesday, had been given three weeks to submit their recommendations.
